events.title: ‘I thank God for killing me and bringing me back’: Nicolas Winding Refn on the emergency op that inspired his new sci-fi horror

sources.title: ‘I thank God for killing me and bringing me back’: Nicolas Winding Refn on the emergency op that inspired his new sci-fi horror
sources.description: Notorious for ultra-violent movies like Drive and The Neon Demon, the Dane had lost the will to direct until ‘the Tom Cruise of surgeons’ saved his life – and triggered an astonishing creative rebirth Nicolas Winding Refn has his phone out, showing me one of the goriest scenes he’s ever been involved in. Given that the Danish director’s movies have involved hands getting sliced off, eyeballs being gouged out and a son reaching deep inside his mother’s womb, that’s certainly saying something. In this video, the camera is fixed upon a beating heart when suddenly – slash! – it gets sliced open with a knife. We travel into the open chamber, as needles arrive to pierce through the muscle. Unsettling and compelling, could this be a future Palme d’Or winner? Unlikely. You see, Refn isn’t the director of this footage; he’s actually the guy lying conked out in the operating room while a surgeon attends to him. Requesting that someone films your own heart surgery is a very Nicolas Winding Refn thing to do. “At first they said no,” says the film-maker known for Drive, Bronson and The Neon Demon. “But then they said, ‘As it’s you, we’ll record it.’” Continue reading...

events.title: Faster! Louder! Brighter! How the attention economy overwhelmed children’s TV

sources.title: Faster! Louder! Brighter! How the attention economy overwhelmed children’s TV
sources.description: Does your child’s favourite show give them a chance to reflect, or does it move too quickly for its lessons to sink in? A version of this piece was originally published on Aeon as The bombarding of childhood I am at the airport gate waiting to depart, watching passengers hurry past with rolling suitcases and paper cups of coffee. A small boy sits very still beside his mother. He holds an iPad close to his chest, almost in a cramp, clutching the screen as if it might otherwise run away. I hear loud clapping hands and squeaking children’s voices. I lean over and see a cartoon character in green snatch a toy from another character in pink. The pink character begins to cry, tears splashing like sprinkles from its enormous eyes. The green character shouts sorry. Instantly, the tears stop and a wide smile replaces them before I have blinked. And, before I have even worked out whether the characters are speaking English or Arabic (as the mother does to the boy), the scene has changed and the two characters are rowing a boat with a random song in the background. The boy’s eyes dart on the screen from right to left, centre, down. His body is still but his attention is being hurried from cue to cue. This is the problem I have come to think of as the pace of children’s media. Continue reading...

sources.description: 9月15日，第二十五届中国国际酒业博览会及中国酒业协会理性饮酒宣传周新闻发布会暨媒体恳谈会在北京举行。会议宣布，第二十五届中国国际酒业博览会将于2026年10月16日至18日在武汉国际博览中心举办，展会主题为“世界名酒 共享荣耀”。同期，2026中国酒业协会理性饮酒宣传周将正式启动，主会场启动仪式暨2026酒业ESG大会定于10月15日下午在武汉国际博览中心举行。中国酒业协会秘书长何勇、武汉市商务局会展处处长王安、贵州习酒投资控股集团有限责任公司党委副书记、副董事长、总经理万波等出席发布会。
